name: Crucible Industries Titan-500 'Earthquake'
description:
The Crucible Industries Titan-500 is a five-shot double-action revolver chambered in .500 S&W Magnum — the most powerful conventional handgun cartridge in production. The frame is investment-cast stainless steel with integral compensator ports in the barrel that redirect muzzle gases upward to counteract the cartridge's extraordinary recoil. Even with the compensator, firing the Titan-500 is a physical event that requires both hands, locked wrists, and a firm stance.

The .500 S&W Magnum round was designed for a world that no longer exists — specifically, for hunting large dangerous game in wilderness that has since been developed or abandoned. In GLMZ, the cartridge's original purpose is irrelevant. What matters is that the round delivers energy levels normally associated with rifle cartridges from a handheld platform, making it effective against targets that shrug off conventional pistol calibers: heavily augmented individuals, improvised armored vehicles, barricade materials, and the rare biological threats that inhabit the peripheral wastelands.

The Earthquake is an absurd weapon by most reasonable standards. It is too heavy for comfortable carry, too powerful for most encounters, and too slow to reload for sustained engagements. But for the specific situations where nothing else in a handgun will do — and those situations do exist in GLMZ's margins — the Titan-500 is the answer to a question nobody wanted to ask.
specifications: caliber: .500 S&W Magnum effective_range: 50 meters rate_of_fire: Double-action revolver magazine_capacity: 5 rounds (cylinder) weight: 2.1 kg
tactical_use: An extreme-power revolver for engagements against heavily armored, augmented, or otherwise resistant targets. The .500 S&W Magnum round penetrates light vehicle armor and defeats most personal body armor through sheer energy transfer. Recoil is extreme even with the compensator — follow-up shots require significant recovery time. Best deployed as a first-shot weapon against high-value hard targets.
cultural_context: The Earthquake is a conversation piece, a tool of last resort, and a symbol of excess depending on context. Owning one marks someone as either a professional who faces extraordinary threats, or an enthusiast with more money than sense. In either case, producing a Titan-500 in any social setting immediately changes the dynamic.
story_hooks: An Earthquake round is found embedded in the wall of a Spire apartment — fired from outside the building, through reinforced glass, from a distance that shouldn't be possible with a handgun. The angle suggests the shooter was at ground level, two hundred meters away.

A bounty hunter carries a Titan-500 loaded with five different specialty rounds, each one for a different type of target. When one round goes missing, the target it was designed for needs to be warned.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist study in industrial excess—a massive stainless steel revolver that dominates the hand with aggressive, purposeful geometry. The frame is substantially larger than conventional pistols, with a noticeably thick barrel assembly crowned by angular compensator vents that cut upward like a predatory maw. The overall impression is one of barely-contained kinetic energy: heavy, deliberate, and uncompromising.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 25.4 cm | Barrel length: 12.7 cm | Frame width: 5.8 cm | Cylinder diameter: 4.9 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Genuinely hefty—2.1 kg of pure metallurgical presence that demands respect in the hand. Not unbalanced, but decidedly front-heavy; the barrel assembly and compensator create a palpable sense of mass that requires confident grip and positioning.
physical_description.primary_material: Investment-cast stainless steel throughout frame, barrel, and cylinder. Reinforced steel internals rated for sustained .500 S&W pressures.
physical_description.finish: Brushed stainless steel with a matte protective coating that resists corrosion and fingerprints. The compensator vents feature slightly darker parkerizing to reduce glare. Minor machining marks visible at contact points—functional, not cosmetic.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray-silver stainless with darker steel accents. No decorative elements or anodizing; pure industrial aesthetic.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip panel (dark gray with slight grip-tape texture) over underlying steel frame. Knurled grip safety lever. The backstrap is bare brushed steel for maximum surface contact.
distinctive_features: Prominent angular compensator ports cut into the top 5cm of barrel—four vertical vents designed to redirect muzzle gases upward
Oversized trigger guard accommodating gloved trigger finger
Heavily reinforced frame shoulders where cylinder pin interfaces
Cylinder has pronounced fluting to reduce weight without sacrificing strength
Exposed mainspring housing with visible coil spring
Adjustable rear sight with wide notch for rapid target acquisition
Ejector rod mechanism is thicker than conventional revolvers, with visible locking collar
Muzzle face is recessed to accommodate full cartridge diameter
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Industries logo (stylized interlocking 'C' and 'I') stamped on left frame above trigger guard. 'TITAN-500' inscribed in block letters on right barrel. '.500 S&W MAGNUM' chamber designation stamped on frame left side. Serial number plate (brushed stainless insert) mounted on grip frame bottom. Heavy weapons permit registration codes laser-etched on cylinder face.
physical_description.condition_typical: Typically field-worn but well-maintained. Light scratches on stainless finish from gear contact and holster wear. Slight discoloration around compensator vents from powder residue and heat cycling. Well-oiled action with no visible rust. Owners tend to baby these—too expensive and powerful to neglect.
